# Independent exact-SHA review — FAIL

Reviewed revision: `3a504670654d1507d6bbc4f3dc02e808a77454f4`

Immutable before revision: `d49fea41cc383dc70d465903e94598a6dc790bd1`

Reviewer session: `hasteless-assistant-verdin` (`64f3-e45c-2dcf-44ed`)

The reviewer did not author, modify, amend, rebase, or push this revision. All 24 declared prose blocks were independently inspected against their adjacent executable contracts and current consumers.

Structural evidence passes: exactly 24 allowlisted blocks across exactly 8 paths changed; every block shrank (1,800 -> 570 words); normalized non-docstring ASTs, inline comments, directive tokens/attachments, unlisted prose, and `HEAD^..HEAD` path scope are exact. Scoped Ruff, format, comment hygiene, and diff-integrity checks pass, and all 26 focused tests pass. The worktree remains clean at the reviewed SHA. Full repository verification was omitted under the operator documentation-only CI waiver.

## Blocking documentation-accuracy finding

`3a504670654d1507d6bbc4f3dc02e808a77454f4:tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_split_jql_queries.py:L6` says that this module's tests assert "cross-query deduplication." They do not. The module contains only the ordering test at L65, Done-cap test at L104, and active-uncapped test at L137. Its fixture also generates disjoint `DIG-ACT-*` and `DIG-DONE-*` keys at L54, so no key can repeat across the two queries and exercise deduplication. The immutable-before module docstring at `d49fea41cc383dc70d465903e94598a6dc790bd1:tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_split_jql_queries.py:L1` did not make this unsupported assertion.

Remediation is comments-only: revise the module docstring to stop claiming that cross-query deduplication is asserted, or accurately state that the distinct fixture prefixes keep these ordering/cap tests separate from cross-query deduplication.

Per the ticket protocol, this finding means no TSV PASS receipt is posted for this SHA. After amendment, rerun the independent review against the new exact SHA.
